newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end pulled down by futures.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end pulled down by futures.

text.p: South African stocks slid on Tuesday as strong equity futures trade pulled the market lower and initial support from a buoyant morning industrials sector faded away in the afternoon.

The day started with the overall index caught between a sinking gold sector, hamstrung by fears over falling bullion prices, and a industrials shares kick-started by Wall Street's surprise Monday rally.
But, dealers said, bears had won the day and industrials started to sink into the red as the afternoon wore on. "The whole market was down as futures retreated," one dealer said.
The overall index ended down 28.3 points to 6,788.8 as industrials, which opened higher, sank to close at 8,010.4, down 12.6 points.

It was a fall in the futures market ahead of the close of the September contract on Monday that did the real damage as futures traders scrambled to settle their positions creating a flow of heavy trade.
"The volumes were really quite fair for a Tuesday," said one dealer.
The all-share September contract was at 6,305/14 from 6,351 and the industrials contract was at 7,782/87 from 7,833.

Gold shares suffered from more bullion prices worries as in the morning London gold fixed at $382.45, its lowest level since July 9, 1996, after a New York sell-off on Monday rippled through Asia into Europe.
The gold share index ended at 1,724.7, down 43.5 points. Gold futures also fell to 1,190/97 from 1,213.
Gold shares suffered as Randgold fell 150 cents to 34.50 rand and Vaal Reefs dipped 11.50 rand to 377.00 rand.
One strong performing share was Richemont which gained more on its recent Nethold television deal to put on 25 cents to close at 69.75 rand.

Dealers were split as to whether futures trade would continue to dominate for the rest of the week. Some said most dealers' had settled their positions and the index would now start to track Wall Street, while others predicted it would still react strongly to the futures sector.
